newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Danish DFDS optimistic about 1996.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Danish DFDS optimistic about 1996.

text.p: Danish shipping line DFDS, subsidiary of J. Lauritzen shipping group reiterated on Friday its optimism about achieving a "very satisfactory" whole year 1996 result.
"When we issued our first-half 1996 result last August, we expressed optimism about achieving very satisfactory earnings for the whole year, DFDS managing director Niels Bach told Reuters.
"If we did not still expect this we would have made a fresh announcement by now," he added.
Bach declined to give any actual estimate but noted that DFDS' Scandinavian Seaways experienced an impressive increase in passenger volume on its Oslo-Copenhagen route last year.
"Our market share in Norway is certainly not declining. We noted increasing passenger figures out of Norway last year," he said.
He said DFDS had no plans to put in highspeed ferries on the Oslo-Copenhagen route like Norwegian competitor Color Lines.

"The Oslo-Copenhagen route is too long for that form of ferry transportation. Highspeed craft are too uncomfortable for passengers on such a route. If you want to get quickly from Oslo to Copenhagen you should fly," Bach said.

Last August DFDS posted interim profits of 61 million crowns, compared to a first-half 1995 loss of 25 million crowns. The unit's profits fell to 82 million crowns for whole year 1995 from the previous year's 271 million crown surplus.
J. Lauritzen is expected to announce its full year 1996 result at the end of March. --Uffe Hansen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
